messages:
Dev Patel: Got an inbound from Support queue — customer asking: “Can you put the Dedicated throughput guarantee in writing?” They want something they can attach to procurement review. 

Dev Patel: Before I respond, can someone confirm which Dedicated tiers have *written* throughput commitments vs “best effort” language? Also do we have the latest approved wording?

Owen Phillips: Do we know which customer/account? And are they already on Dedicated or still evaluating?

Dev Patel: Not yet live, currently evaluating Dedicated. They’re asking for “tokens/sec guaranteed” language. Sales is looped but they sent the question to Support email alias.

Rachel Kim: This is coming up a lot w/ enterprise. We should be consistent: Standard shouldn’t promise a written throughput floor, right?

Lauren Bishop: Yep. Current policy from the tiering doc: 
- Standard: no contractual throughput guarantee (we can share sizing guidance + typical perf, but not as an SLO/creditable commitment)
- Plus: includes written throughput SLO for the deployment (floor measured over window, subject to exclusions)
- Premium: includes written throughput SLO + stronger posture (warm pool/spares + faster response targets), and is the one we’re comfortable with for “must be in writing” customers.

Lauren Bishop: If they’re asking for it in writing during eval, we can share the *customer-facing* SLO language excerpt, but it needs the usual “subject to contract/order form” disclaimer.

Dev Patel: Great. Do we have a link to the current language? I don’t want to forward an outdated draft.

Elliot Price: Latest approved wording is in the Dedicated docs PR + the MSA addendum draft. Internal link: <https://redwood-internal/wiki/dedicated/throughput-slo-language> (this mirrors what’s going into PM-503). 

Elliot Price: There’s also a short “email-ready” paragraph under “External summary” we wrote for Support/CS.

Sofia Mendes: +1 to Lauren’s tier breakdown. Legal note: please do NOT send the full addendum PDF unless Sales/Deal Desk is coordinating. Support can send the *non-binding summary* + point them to Sales for contractual language.

Sofia Mendes: Also avoid stating specific numeric tokens/sec in email unless it’s a quote tied to a specific shape + model + region (and even then it should come from Sales quoting + order form). The safer phrasing is “throughput floor as defined in the order form for Plus/Premium.”

Dev Patel: Understood. So reply should be: “We can provide written SLO language for Dedicated Plus/Premium; Standard is best-effort,” and route them to Sales for formal paperwork.

Isabelle Laurent: Yes — and if they’re asking for “in writing,” we should treat it as a deal desk trigger. Please @mention Sales Ops / Deal Desk in the thread w/ the account name once you have it.

Owen Phillips: Any nuance around “written commitment” vs “public docs”? Some customers accept public documentation if it’s clear.

Lauren Bishop: We can share public docs for how it’s measured (window/exclusions), but the “commitment + remedy” is only contractual in Plus/Premium. For Standard, docs should say “observed throughput” / “target” and explicitly not a guarantee.

Rachel Kim: Support response: can we standardize the exclusions callout? Customers always ask about what voids it.

Elliot Price: The summary paragraph already mentions the top exclusions at a high level: customer-side throttling, unsupported model/version changes, and planned maintenance windows. If they want details, we can share the FAQ section (still non-binding).

Dev Patel: Can someone paste the exact email-ready paragraph here so I can respond quickly?

Elliot Price: Here’s the current Support-safe snippet (non-binding):

Elliot Price: “For Redwood Dedicated, throughput commitments (where included) are defined as a minimum sustained throughput floor measured over a rolling window, subject to documented exclusions (e.g., customer-side throttling, unsupported model/version or configuration changes, and planned maintenance). Written throughput SLO commitments are available with Dedicated Plus and Dedicated Premium and are finalized in the applicable order form/addendum. Dedicated Standard includes performance guidance and monitoring, but does not include a contractual throughput guarantee.”

Dev Patel: Perfect.

Sofia Mendes: Add one sentence: “Any specific numbers/thresholds are tied to the deployment’s region, model, and hardware shape and will be provided by your Redwood account team.” Keeps us out of trouble.

Dev Patel: Will do.

Owen Phillips: Also: if they’re already seeing perf concerns in a POC, let’s avoid framing it as “we missed SLO” since they’re not on a tier w/ SLO yet. Just offer to run a benchmark + sizing.

Lauren Bishop: +1. If they’re in a regulated procurement (sounds like it), default recommend Premium for the “in writing” ask.

Rachel Kim: Dev — once you get the account name, tag me. CS can help align expectations on escalation path too.

Dev Patel: Acknowledged. I’m replying now with the snippet + routing to Sales for contractual language. Will follow up with account details.

Dev Patel: (Reaction) :thumbsup: 

Dev Patel: Update: customer is asking if “Plus” is sufficient or if only “Premium” includes the written guarantee.

Lauren Bishop: Clarify: Plus includes written throughput SLO (same measurement semantics), Premium adds stronger operational entitlements (warm pool/spares, failover posture, faster response). If they only care about “in writing,” Plus qualifies; if they care about tighter response/ops, Premium.

Sofia Mendes: Exactly. Phrase it as: “Both Plus and Premium include written throughput SLO language; Premium includes enhanced operational commitments.”

Dev Patel: Great. Sending that clarification now + pointing them to Sales to choose tier and finalize terms.
